scope: synthetic real CLI capacity; loopback provider, no paid calls or task-quality claim
memory_measurement: GNU time maximum per-process RSS of the command and waited-for children; not simultaneous process-tree memory
provider: Scripted loopback SSE; no paid model calls
scope_notes: Current executable includes lexical JSON admission and lossless journal preflight; all executable and fixture bytes were snapshotted before the run.
Allowance was set to 1200 seconds before execution. The prior report used 600 seconds and an older executable; these single shared-host runs are not a controlled latency benchmark.
The next model attempt reservation was durable, but its intent exceeded journal capacity; no corresponding provider request occurred.
The preserved prefix remains inspectable and replayable. No terminal outcome could be saved; this does not show that a full journal can resume.
Compaction was deliberately disabled for this synthetic capacity measurement. Task-quality and sustained compaction/restart trials are separate.
The runner revalidates the full journal on each append. This run exposes that cumulative cost; it is not a throughput guarantee.
